Olympian reports: A dismal tale - in fact the most dismal that has been recorded for any Brighton Relay for over 30 years.
by OLYMPIAN A great day for Belgrave with a win on the Brighton road for the first time since 1952.
by Olympian Rarely does the weather let us down for London to Brighton Relays, but on this occasion, it could hardly have been worse.

With a little more experience of the course, we could probably have improved on our performance slightly which might have produced a win, but Coventry thoroughly deserved their victory with some extremely good running; as befits the National Road Relay Champions. Olympian
Rimmer and Baker came in 105th and 131st to make a team score of 267 points which gave us 7th place. Olympian
Their last man was few places in front of Charlie Walker - perhaps Jack Brown may have a twinge of conscience for withdrawing just to let Charlie run ! Olympian
"Olympian's" report on this fighting effort is recorded elsewhere in this issue. So two firsts, two seconds, one fifth and one sixth is the final summary for Autumn 1966.

First a win in the National Cross Country and then the National Road Relay to be run in Leicester on April 1st 1967 - the additional four stages in this race are to our advantage but only if everyone likely to be selected makes this his aim - we have the runners but names are no good without complete fitness. Olympian
On the whole a satisfactory performance but being beaten is always disappointing - we no longer expect this to happen to us Olympian
